Thanks Rishi — attaching the first pass.\nAttachments included: redwood_field_mapping_v1.csv (mapping + redaction notes), redwood_dataflow_v3.png (annotated), and a short note on telemetry pseudonymization.\nQuick summary: \n- Ingest tier (proxy): sees full raw inputs for routing/normalization; we apply optional client-side masking if requested in config.\n- Preprocessing layer: performs tokenization; raw PII is retained in memory for inference but not persisted unless the customer enables logging.\n- Model runtime: KV cache retains recent tokens for session performance (TTL configurable). Cache entries are encrypted at rest with customer-scoped KMS keys for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS with strict access controls.\n- Telemetry/logs: default telemetry scrubs full identifiers. Non-scrubbed telemetry is only enabled under explicit customer opt-in and is stored in a separate export bucket with limited retention.\n- Subprocessors: short list in the CSV (CloudInfraCo — hosting/bare-metal in us-west, CacheOps — cache management in us-east, BackupVault — archival, located in us). Full residency column included.\n
Open items:\n- Connor: can you confirm the diagram's arrow labeled "export pipeline" is accurate for our hosted edge? I noted a possible onshore transfer step there.\n- Laura: we'll need copy for the DPA annex about KMS custody options and a recommended sentence about subprocessors.\n
Marissa
Product Security

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple legal notes for the DPA annex and SSQ response: \n- Subprocessors: we can disclose the current roster and residency, but avoid categorical promises about future subprocessors. Recommend: "Redwood discloses subprocessors on a best-effort basis and will provide notice of material changes per the DPA."\n- KMS language: provide two short bullets for customer options — (1) Redwood-managed KMS (default) with documented access controls and (2) customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private customers; include statement that key custody is auditable and that we provide exportable KMS attestation artifacts on request.\n- Exports/pseudonymization: include the existing telemetry opt-in sentence and call out that we offer a pseudonymization pipeline (deterministic tokenization) for customers that require shorter-term linkage without storing raw values.\n
I'll draft the suggested DPA annex paragraph and attach redlines to the DPA candidate doc. Also flagging that if FinEdge requires explicit onshore-only processing for production traffic, that's a commercial change to escalate to Sales/AMs for capacity planning.\n
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
